preamble.summary: Proverbs 8 is Lady Wisdom's major-self-testimony — the PROTO-LOGOS poem of the Hebrew Bible. After Wisdom calls out in the city (vv. 1–11) and self-describes her role with kings (vv. 12–21), she utters the theologically-explosive claim: 'the LORD possessed me at the beginning of his way … when he established the heavens I was there … I was beside him, like a master workman' (vv. 22–31). This passage became the central battleground of the Arian controversy: was Wisdom (read-Christologically) CREATED (Arius, reading Prov 8:22 LXX 'the Lord CREATED me, ektisen me') or BEGOTTEN (Athanasius, reading the Hebrew qanani as 'acquired/possessed')? The Nicene Creed's 'begotten, not made' (gennēthenta, ou poiēthenta) responds directly to this LXX reading.
preamble.notable_variants: 8:22 'the LORD created/possessed me at the beginning' — THE ARIAN CONTROVERSY'S CENTRAL TEXT (Arius cited the LXX ektisen as proof Christ was created); 8:30 'master workman' (amon / harmozousa) beside God at creation; the entire vv. 22–31 as proto-Logos poem grounding John 1:1 and Col 1:15–18 Christology.
preamble.structural_notes: MT Prov 8 = LXX Prov 8. 36 verses. Wisdom's autobiography.

verses.mt_rendering: The LORD possessed me at the beginning of his way, before his works of old
verses.variant_rendering: The Lord created me as the beginning of his ways, for his works
variant_notes: ARIAN-CONTROVERSY'S CENTRAL TEXT. The LXX's ektisen me ('he CREATED me') — where MT's qanani is ambiguous between 'created' and 'possessed/acquired' — became the single-most-disputed word in the fourth-century Christological debates. Arius (d. 336) cited this verse to argue that the Son-of-God (identified-with-Wisdom-here) was CREATED, a creature-of-the-Father, subordinate. Athanasius (d. 373) responded that the Hebrew qanani means 'possessed' — that Wisdom was BEGOTTEN, not made.

THE NICENE RESPONSE. The Nicene Creed (325 AD, revised Constantinople 381) specifically-addresses this verse with the formula 'gennēthenta, ou poiēthenta, homoousion tō patri' — 'begotten, not made, of the same essence as the Father.' The 'not made' (ou poiēthenta) is the direct-rebuttal of Arius's reading of ektisen me. Nicene Christology reads the Prov 8 LXX as applying to the Son's-being-sent-into-creation-for-economic-roles, not to his eternal-essence.

BROADER CHRISTOLOGICAL BACKGROUND. Colossians 1:15–18's 'firstborn of all creation … in him all things were created … he is before all things' and John 1:1–3's 'in the beginning was the Logos … all things were made through him' — both work through the Prov 8 Wisdom-tradition. Hebrews 1:3's 'exact imprint of his nature' also engages Wisdom's-eternal-generation.
'Ages ago I was set up, at the first, before the beginning of the earth' tracks MT. PRE-EARTH existence — Wisdom (Christologically-read) predates creation.
'When there were no depths I was brought forth, when there were no springs abounding with water' tracks MT.
'Before the mountains had been shaped, before the hills, I was brought forth' tracks MT.
'Before he had made the earth with its fields, or the first of the dust of the world' tracks MT.
'When he established the heavens, I was there; when he drew a circle on the face of the deep' tracks MT. I-WAS-THERE witness-at-creation.
'When he made firm the skies above, when he established the fountains of the deep' tracks MT.
'When he assigned to the sea its limit, so that the waters might not transgress his command, when he marked out the foundations of the earth' tracks MT.

'Then I was beside him, like a master workman, and I was daily his delight, rejoicing before him always' tracks MT. MASTER-WORKMAN (amon in MT, harmozousa in LXX — 'one who puts together, harmonizer'). The Hebrew amon could mean 'craftsman,' 'nursling,' or 'architect.' Colossians 1:16 ('by him all things were created … all things were created through him and for him') reads this Christologically: Christ-as-Wisdom-beside-the-Father creates the cosmos.

'Rejoicing in his inhabited world and delighting in the children of man' tracks MT. DELIGHTING-IN-HUMANS. Christologically read: the Son's pre-incarnation delight in humanity anticipates the incarnation. John 1:14 ('the Word became flesh and dwelt among us') fulfills the delight-in-the-children-of-man.
'And now, O sons, listen to me: blessed are those who keep my ways' tracks MT.
'Hear instruction and be wise, and do not neglect it' tracks MT.
'Blessed is the one who listens to me, watching daily at my gates, waiting beside my doors' tracks MT. WATCHING-AT-MY-GATES wisdom-discipleship.
'For whoever finds me finds life and obtains favor from the LORD' tracks MT. WHOEVER-FINDS-ME-FINDS-LIFE. John 14:6 ('I am the way, the truth, and the LIFE') Christologically fulfills.

'But he who fails to find me injures himself; all who hate me love death' tracks MT. HATE-ME-LOVE-DEATH closing. Revelation 22:17's 'whoever is thirsty come / the one who desires, take the water of life without price' invites instead.
